meanings.en: to choose, select; to use up completely (quotas, limits)
meanings.note: + acc. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to choose, use up', paired with 'выбирать'.

examples.text: В этом году все квоты выбрали.
examples.trans: This year all the quotas have been used up.
She chose the most beautiful dress.
Agreed, I will choose a movie.

meanings.note: Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.

meanings.note: Громкая связь = speakerphone. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('loud; high-profile').

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лгожданный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('long-awaited').

examples.trans: And now the long-awaited moment has arrived.

examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'мечательный'). Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('wonderful, remarkable').

examples.text: Все наши юные творцы сделали замечательные поделки!

meanings.en: to earn, to deserve, to merit

meanings.note: in 'рабочее место' = workplace, job

наступить.gloss: to come (of time); to step on

meanings.en: to come, to set in (night, winter, a moment)
meanings.note: Наступила ночь = night has fallen. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ступить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come (of time); to step on', paired with 'наступать'.

Наступить на + accusative. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ступить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come (of time); to step on', paired with 'наступать'.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъявить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to announce, declare', paired with 'объявлять'.

examples.text: Перед тем, как я объявлю победителя, внимание!

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Let's give a round of applause to all our participants!

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ложный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('complicated, difficult').

examples.trans: Danila, let's go. Look, there's nothing complicated.

стараться.gloss: to try, to make an effort

meanings.en: to try hard, to make an effort
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тараться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try, to make an effort', paired with 'постараться'.

examples.trans: He always tries to help his friends.

examples.text: Марина, зря вы стараетесь. Он никогда не уйдёт от своей Аллы Евгеньевны.
examples.trans: Marina, you're trying in vain. He will never leave his Alla Evgenyevna.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'creator' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: An artist is a creator of beauty.

examples.text: Все наши юные творцы сделали замечательные поделки!
examples.trans: All our young creators made wonderful crafts!

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: The one over there. Core Russian det meaning 'that' in everyday speech.

Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.
